summary: Junyang Lin introduces the Qwen series and the team's dream of building a generalist agent model, sharing key resources: Qwen Chat, the technical blog, and open-source checkpoints. The narrative progresses through Qwen2.5-Max, competitive with Claude 3.5, GPT-4o, and DeepSeek V3, which served as a foundation for RL research that improved AIME 2024 scores from ~65 to ~80 for a 32B model. Qwen3 was released in multiple dense and MoE sizes: a 235B/22B-active MoE flagship competitive with o3-mini, a 30B/3B-active MoE, and a 4B distilled model competitive with the prior 72B flagship, deployable on mobile. The standout hybrid thinking mode combines thinking and non-thinking in a single model—claimed as a first in open source—with dynamic thinking budgets trading accuracy for token efficiency. Qwen3 supports 119 languages and enhances agent capabilities including MCP support and tool use during thinking. On the multimodal side, Qwen2.5-VL excels on benchmarks like MMMU and MathVista, QVQ explores thinking in vision-language models, and Qwen2.5-Omni accepts text, vision, and audio inputs, generating text and audio. Qwen2.5-Omni achieves state-of-the-art audio performance for 7B-class models and surprisingly surpasses Qwen2.5-VL 7B on vision-language understanding, though the team acknowledges a performance drop in language and agent tasks they plan to recover through better data and training. The team strongly commits to open sourcing under Apache 2.0, providing quantized models in GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ, and MLX formats, and is building Qwen3 Coders. Products include webdev for generating deployable websites from simple prompts and deep research for comprehensive PDF reports, with RL-based fine-tuning in progress. Looking ahead, the team sees substantial room in pre-training through better data, multimodal data, synthetic data, and potentially RL in pre-training beyond next-token prediction. Scaling laws are shifting from model size and data to compute in RL with long-horizon reasoning and environment feedback. Context scaling targets at least 1M tokens this year, then 10M, toward infinite context. Modality scaling aims to unify understanding and generation, including image generation like GPT-4o. The overarching vision: moving from training models to training agents—the era of agents.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Resources
sections.summary: Junyang Lin introduces himself from the Qwen team and shares key resources: Qwen Chat for multimodal interaction, the technical blog at qwen.github.io, and open-source checkpoints on Hugging Face and code on GitHub.

sections.title: Qwen2.5-Max and Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning
sections.summary: Qwen2.5-Max was competitive with Claude 3.5, GPT-4o, and DeepSeek V3. The team pursued RL for reasoning, with AIME 2024 rising from ~65 to ~80 for a 32B model.

sections.title: Qwen3 Model Sizes and Architecture
sections.summary: Qwen3 released in multiple dense and MoE sizes: 235B/22B-active MoE flagship, 30B/3B-active MoE, and 4B distilled model deployable on mobile.

sections.title: Hybrid Thinking Mode and Dynamic Thinking Budget
sections.summary: Qwen3 combines thinking and non-thinking modes in a single model, controllable via prompts or hyperparameters. Dynamic thinking budgets let users set max thinking tokens, with AIME 2024 scaling from ~40% to ~80%+.

sections.title: Language Support and Agent Capabilities
sections.summary: Qwen3 supports 119 languages and dialects, up from 29. Agent and coding capabilities enhanced with MCP support, enabling tool use during thinking.

sections.title: Open Weights and MoE Strategy
sections.summary: Qwen3 open-weights include 2 MoE and 6 dense models plus desktop models. The 4B targets mobile, the 32B targets local deployment and RL. The team believes MoE is the future trend.

sections.title: Multimodal Models: Qwen2.5-VL, QVQ, and Qwen2.5-Omni
sections.summary: Qwen2.5-VL released January 2025 with strong benchmark results. QVQ explores thinking in vision-language models. Qwen2.5-Omni accepts text, vision, and audio, generating text and audio.

sections.title: Qwen2.5-Omni Performance, Open Source Commitment, and Qwen3 Coders
sections.summary: Qwen2.5-Omni achieves state-of-the-art audio performance for 7B models and surprisingly surpasses Qwen2.5-VL 7B on vision-language understanding, though language and agent task performance needs recovery. The team commits to open sourcing under Apache 2.0 with quantized formats (GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ, MLX). Qwen3 Coders are in development. Models range from 0.6B to 235B, each serving large user bases.

sections.title: Products: WebDev and Deep Research
sections.summary: The webdev feature generates deployable websites from simple prompts (e.g., Twitter website, sunscreen product page, cards from links) with live preview and shareable URLs. Deep research takes a topic, plans, searches step by step, and produces a downloadable PDF report. RL fine-tuning for deep research is in progress.

sections.title: Future Directions: Pre-training, Scaling, Context, Modalities, and the Era of Agents
sections.summary: The team sees much room in pre-training through better data, multimodal data, synthetic data, and potentially RL beyond next-token prediction. Scaling laws are shifting to RL compute with long-horizon reasoning and environment feedback. Context scaling targets 1M+ tokens this year, then 10M, toward infinite. Modality scaling aims to unify understanding and generation. The overarching vision: moving from training models to training agents—the era of agents.
